transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-02 09:00 PDT | Duration approx 48 mins | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Okafor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Brightwell Head of ML), Raj Patel (Brightwell Platform), Sofia Gomez (Brightwell CTO)
Summary: Quick results review from last week's smoke runs, alignment on model staging strategy, tabletop rollback walkthrough and ownership, decide on benchmark cadence and data needed for next run.

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay good morning everyone thanks for joining, um today we want to walk through what we saw last week on the smoke jobs and then run a short tabletop around how we'd perform an emergency rollback if a model degrades.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: thanks Maya, quick note we're on CEST for me is weird but i'm in SF this week so timing worked out, uh the team looked at the transcript logs you sent. couple of immediate flags — hallucination spikes on the 70 ring long-context cases.
[00:38] David Okafor: yeah so to frame it, we ran two variants: rwd-mini-13b-4q (quantized) and a larger llama-3-70b-qlora-ish build we pulled from the catalog. transcription thing: the catalog label came through as "Llamma 3 seventy" in the job output — so ignore the typos there.
[00:55] Raj Patel: just to confirm, the smoke runs used the production traffic replay you provided, right? small subset ~3000 requests, same token distribution?
[01:07] Lena Ortiz: yep 3k across three hour window, we replayed with session distribution and a few long-shot tails. sent the logs to the shared drive, link in chat.
[01:18] Maya Chen: perfect. David, can you summarize the perf numbers? latency p95s, token cost, that sort of thing.
[01:27] David Okafor: sure. p95 for rwd-mini-13b-4q was 420ms, per-token GPU cost baseline about 0.0009 USD per token — that's approximate — memory pressure low, kv cache behaviour looked good. for the bigger 70b qlora variant p95 shot up to 1.6s in our staging infra, cost per token ~0.0032 USD and we saw occasional >3s tails on context lengths beyond 2k tokens. there were also two runs where the model hit a CUDA OOM in our test harness — likely due to slightly different batch packing in the replay.
[02:02] Lena Ortiz: that's consistent with what we saw. the bigger model did better qualitatively on the abstractive summarize prompts but regressed on fact recall prompts — more hallucinations.
[02:12] Sofia Gomez: overall, our success criteria still is under 600ms p95 and hallucination <= 1.5% on our eval set. so the 70b isn't meeting latency nor the hallucination target on that slice.
[02:25] Maya Chen: makes sense. so we have a tradeoff: larger model better on some tasks but fails on our core success metrics and increases cost. SE, David, what would you recommend for staging pin strategy?
[02:38] David Okafor: propose a two-track staging: "canary" route for rwd-mini-13b-4q as the default rolled-up model, and a shadow route for the 70b variant to collect quality metrics without serving live traffic. then a soft-fallback setup that if latency or hallucinations breach thresholds, requests route to cached completions or to a smaller fallback like rwd-7b-conv. we can implement that via Redwood routing rules: per-route thresholds, model_variant fallback, and circuit-breakers.
[03:05] Raj Patel: will that add more network hops? our egress budget is tight and we have to keep VPC peering minimal.
[03:13] David Okafor: minimal. routing is done at the control plane; the actual inference nodes are in the same region. the additional cost is mostly evaluation computation for shadowing — you're not double-serving live responses.
[03:25] Lena Ortiz: one concern: how fast can we flip? if a model starts degrading we need <2 minutes failover to a pinned older model.
[03:34] Maya Chen: good question. David?
[03:36] David Okafor: if we pre-pin the older model in the gateway and warm its KV cache, we can route traffic in under 60s. Realistic timeline: 20-60s depending on KV cache hit rate and tokenization warm-up. if you want guaranteed sub-15s, we'd need pre-populated hot-paths which is more expensive.
[03:55] Sofia Gomez: pre-populating sounds worthwhile for high-risk endpoints only. we can pick top 5 customer-facing routes.
[04:03] Lena Ortiz: yeah let's pick three. one for summarization, one for Q&A, and one for embedded extraction.
[04:09] Maya Chen: noted. David maybe outline the tabletop — who does what if we detect a regression in prod?
[04:17] David Okafor: okay tabletop walkthrough: detection -> triage -> mitigation -> root-cause. detection: monitoring alerts on latency spike + eval-set regression. triage: SE and Brightwell ML lead confirm whether it's model drift vs prompt drift. mitigation: AE/Platform triggers soft-fallback (control plane toggle) and enables shadow rollback. root-cause: collect traces, KV logs and run localized reproduction. We'll need a single pager that maps names to steps.
[04:47] Raj Patel: what's the control plane toggle access model? we need RBAC and audit for compliance.
[04:52] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SSO + SAML and RBAC; audit logs go to your logging endpoint or we can push to S3 for retention. we'll share the SOC2 + audit doc.
[04:59] Lena Ortiz: please do — we have an upcoming internal audit, they'll want that.
[05:04] Maya Chen: noted — action item.
[05:07] [05:07] Maya Chen: quick pause, two small gotchas from the runs: one, our tokenization mismatch — you had an extra prefix in the traffic replay which changed the prompt distribution a bit; two, the catalog labels caused our benchmark harness to pick the wrong qconfig for quantization.
[05:24] Raj Patel: ah the extra prefix was from our session cookie dump script, my bad. can share sanitized version.
[05:29] David Okafor: the qconfig mismatch meant we saw slightly worse latency on the 13b-4q than expected; when we forced the recommended qconfig p95 dropped ~60ms. so small but matters.
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: okay we'll re-run with sanitized traffic and recommended qconfig.
[05:44] Sofia Gomez: on the rollback timeline — do you have a playbook for emergency rollback testing? we want to run a live drill.
[05:51] David Okafor: yes, we'll provide a tabletop playbook. proposed drill timeline: D-7 announce, D-3 run shadow smoke, D-1 warm caches, D day run 30-min controlled traffic and exercise failover. we'll be present to flip routes and monitor.
[06:07] Maya Chen: let's lock D-day for the drill on 2026-07-13 — Raj, can you confirm stakeholders?
[06:12] Raj Patel: i'll confirm by 2026-07-06, but yes prelim yes.
[06:17] Maya Chen: great.
[06:19] [06:19] Lena Ortiz: one more question — encryption and key management. if we use Redwood Private, can we bring our own KMS?
[06:27] Maya Chen: yes, BYOK is supported in Private deployments; for Dedicated we also support customer-managed KMS integrations. we'll put the integration checklist in the shared drive.
[06:36] Sophia Gomez: (interruption) also wondering about degraded-path quality: if we fallback to a smaller model, do we add a tagging layer so we can measure delta in user experience?
[06:45] David Okafor: yes, we add headers/metadata so you can A/B measure. Redwood console will surface per-route cost and latency and you can add a "quality shim" metric that logs delta between primary & fallback.
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: sweet. for our internal metrics team we need the raw token-level breakdowns too.
[07:05] Maya Chen: we'll enable token-level exports for the trial.
[07:09] [07:09] Raj Patel: network question — when you shadow the 70b, that's going to spin up temporary nodes on your infra right? are we charged for shadow compute?
[07:18] David Okafor: yes you incur compute for shadow runs; we can constrict the sample rate to minimize cost and still get statistically meaningful quality signals. we'll give a cost estimate in the benchmark report.
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: can you also run a regression on our embedding vector space? we saw a drift in semantic-sim scores last month.
[07:36] David Okafor: we can, but embeddings are a separate pipeline. Redwood supports embedding-model pinning and rollback similar to generation. recommend separate smoke runs for embeddings.
[07:47] Maya Chen: ok adding that to next steps.
[07:50] [07:50] Sofia Gomez: quick question about rollback safety: do you support "dead man's switch" where we revert if a downstream error rate grows?
[07:58] David Okafor: yes, you can configure automated rollback triggers based on metrics (error-rate, latency, quality) with a circuit breaker. we can demo that in the drill.
[08:06] Lena Ortiz: excellent.
[08:08] Maya Chen: last thing — prompts. we propose holding a prompt-stability window during the drill: freeze prompt templates for 48 hours so we can attribute regressions to the model not prompt changes.
[08:18] Raj Patel: agreed.
[08:20] Maya Chen: wrap-up — recap of agreed items: 1) Redwood to run targeted benchmark with sanitized traffic and recommended qconfig and share CSVs by 2026-07-09; 2) Customer to share canonical prompts and failing-case logs by 2026-07-06; 3) Lock tabletop drill for 2026-07-13 and finalize invite list; 4) Redwood to share SOC2/SAML/KMS integration docs and the rollback playbook.
[08:44] Lena Ortiz: thanks all — feel like we're in a good place. small ask: can we also see a quick run of the p95 heatmap across regions?
[08:53] David Okafor: yes, will include regional p95s.
[08:56] Maya Chen: i'll follow up in email with links and the action item tracker. thanks everyone for the time.
[09:02] Sofia Gomez: bye all.
